root_cause.text: The functions `vidtv_ts_null_write_into()` and `vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into()` pass their argument structs by value, causing unnecessary stack copies that include uninitialized data (e.g., padding or uninitialized fields), which triggers MSAN uninit-value warnings.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes both function signatures from passing structs by value (`struct null_packet_write_args args`, `struct pcr_write_args args`) to passing them by const pointer (`const struct null_packet_write_args *args`, `const struct pcr_write_args *args`). The CVE description states that passing by value “causing MSAN to report uninit-value warnings” and the fix “avoid[s] the stack copy of the struct along with its MSAN shadow and origin metadata.”
